subject: Orchid Systems SIG questionnaire — evidence collection plan
messages:
From: Elena Petrova <elena@orchid-systems.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orchid-systems.com
Date: 2027-06-21T08:13:00+01:00
Subject: Orchid Systems SIG questionnaire and evidence intake

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the quick intro call this morning. Attached is our completed SIG spreadsheet (Orchid_SIG_v3.xlsx) and our procurement terms PDF for your legal and security teams to review. We have a few timing constraints on our side: the procurement committee wants an initial control substantiation package by July 5th, and our security reviewers would like to see supporting artifacts (logs, diagrams, policies) shortly after.

Couple of quick questions so we can map responsibilities on our side:
- Do you prefer artifacts uploaded to a shared Google Drive folder or an encrypted SFTP drop?
- Can Redwood provide a mapping template (control -> expected artifact type) so our engineering and security teams can collate evidence quickly?
- Are there any controls in the SIG where Redwood will need to provide a signed attestation vs. just an artifact?

We can do a short kickoff next week; I propose Tue/Wed morning (CEST) — what works for your team?

Attachments: Orchid_SIG_v3.xlsx, orchid_procurement_terms.pdf

Thanks,
Elena Petrova
Head of IT Risk | Orchid Systems
elena@orchid-systems.com
+44 20 7946 0XXX

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-06-21T09:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Orchid Systems SIG questionnaire and evidence intake

Elena —

Appreciate the packet and the clear timeline. Quick reply with a proposed intake plan so we can align on owners and deadlines:

1) Intake channel: we prefer a shared Drive folder for initial exchange, with a separate SFTP option for any encrypted forensic logs. I will share a Drive link and a short upload guide by EOD.
2) Mapping template: attached is our "Redwood_SIG_onboarding-guide.pdf" which includes a control->artifact mapping CSV template that Jasmine will use to coordinate evidence collection.
3) Attestations vs artifacts: generally we provide artifacts for most SIG controls; for a small subset (KMS key custody, SOC 2 attestations) we can provide signed statements — Kimberly, I left the subset notes to you (see below).

Proposed schedule:
- Kickoff (30 min): Wed 2027-06-23 at 09:00 CEST or 14:00 CEST (pick one)
- Artifact intake window: 2027-06-24 — 2027-07-02 (primary upload)
- Evidence review & clarifying asks: 2027-07-03 — 2027-07-06

If that works, I will create the Drive folder, invite your procurement and engineering contacts, and assign internal owners.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Office +1 415 555 01XX

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Petrova <elena@orchid-systems.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-22T11:30:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Orchid Systems SIG questionnaire and evidence intake — artifact expectations and owners

Elena / Marcus,

Thanks for initiating this. A few clarifying points from the Security & Compliance side to make artifact collection efficient. I split asks into "high priority" (needed for control substantiation by your July 5 target) and "supplemental" (helpful for deeper review but not blocking).

High priority (deliver by 2027-07-02):
- KMS key custody diagram (architecture-level) and key rotation policy (PDF).
- Sample key rotation event log (redacted); ideally the last rotation cycle trace (7 days of logs).
- Evidence for access control: sample IAM role definitions and a list of privileged admin accounts with role-owner contact.
- Recent SOC 2 report (if you require cross-references to our attestations) — we will provide the standard SOC 2 letter and control narrative.

Supplemental (deliver by 2027-07-09):
- Telemetry example: tokenized runtime telemetry snippet showing request-to-response latency per model variant (sample 24-hour window). Redact any customer identifiers.
- Data flow diagram showing ingress/egress boundaries and any 3rd-party data processors.
- Incident response playbook excerpt for containment/forensics (redacted names ok).

Upload guidance: please put each artifact in the Drive folder under a named subfolder that matches the SIG control ID (we will share the template CSV, e.g., SIG-1.2_authz -> artifact.pdf). For large log dumps we can provide an SFTP endpoint — flag those files with prefix ORCH_LOG_ so our collectors pick them up.

Owner notes (internal): Jasmine will own the template and the Drive layout; Marcus will own the procurement/legal touchpoints; I will own attestations and technical clarifications.

Happy to discuss on the kickoff. Marcus — please share the Drive link and proposed times.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
